# A paired-roof obstruction to the limiting ordinary physical stress

This is a bounded geometric consequence of the newly vanishing physical
buffer corrections. It gives an ACTUAL body motion whose response can be
tested using only the limiting convex physical-speed inequality. It is
not a centroid-hull contraction or a payment by gradient-class mass.

The conclusion requires a specified proper cap-trace geometry on the
moving roof faces. A weak limiting surface measure does not automatically
retain that geometry. No general existence theorem for the roof motion,
nor an arbitrary-n,d OC proof, is claimed.

## 1. Actual finite support-plane motions of a paired roof

Let D be a compact convex horizontal body in base/continuous coordinates
(z,X), with complete finite sampled base P and positive horizontal fibers
B_z in dimension d-1. In dimension d=1 use a singleton B_z of measure1.
Let

    H(z)=min_(r=1,...,m) a_r(z)>0

on the base projection, with each a_r affine. Form the actual convex body

    C={(z,X,y):(z,X) in D, -H(z)<=y<=H(z)}.

Its sampled fibers are the genuine prisms B_z times [-H_z,H_z]. Let b_r
be nonnegative affine functions on the base projection. For small t>=0,

    H_t(z)=min_r [a_r(z)-t b_r(z)]

remains positive and concave and gives an actual nested convex body C_t.
At each sampled base define

    h_z=max{b_r(z):a_r(z)=H(z)}>=0.

Because P and the affine family are finite, for all sufficiently small
t the exact sampled heights are H_t(z)=H_z-t h_z. Thus the original
removed mass is exactly tD, where

    D=2 sum_z h_z |B_z|.                               (1)

Here and below mass means the ORIGINAL mixed measure
mu(S)=sum_(z in P) vol_d(S_z), and boundary integration means the sum
of the d-dimensional fibers' (d-1)-dimensional surface integrals.

The inward boundary speed is h_z on the upper and lower horizontal roof
faces and zero on side faces, apart from their surface-null intersections.
Assume D>0.

This speed is not being declared a globally convex function. To access it
through the limiting convex test cone, use the genuine convex functions

    Phi_R=max(0,
              max_r [b_r(z)-R(a_r(z)-y)],
              max_r [b_r(z)-R(a_r(z)+y)]).              (2)

All old gaps a_r(z)+/-y are nonnegative on C. Consequently Phi_R decreases
boundedly as R increases, and on surface-almost-every boundary point its
limit is exactly the stated roof speed v. On a roof face only active
support planes remain, giving max_active b_r=h_z; away from both roofs,
every gap is strictly positive. Thus for every bounded surface density W,

    int_boundary (W-beta)Phi_R -> int_boundary(W-beta)v. (3)

This is dominated convergence on the ACTUAL boundary. To contradict a
limiting convex-test inequality, first choose one finite R for which the
right response remains strictly positive; only then use that fixed test
in the buffer limit. No equality at finite R is presumed.

## 2. Exact half-loss cap geometry

Suppose a finite actual cap menu has nonnegative weights omega_j summing
to1. On each moving fiber h_z>0, assume each cap's continuous y component
is nonzero and its cutting graph crosses the ENTIRE prism strictly:

    -H_z < q_j(z,X) < H_z  for every X in B_z,

where its boundary is y=q_j(z,X). Finite compactness gives a positive
margin, so these strict inequalities persist under small roof shrinkage.
Every such cap contains exactly one of the two moving roof points at
each X. Therefore, irrespective of its orientation or weight,

    W_z(X,H_z)+W_z(X,-H_z)=1,                           (4)

where W is the actual weighted captured-side boundary load. Every cap
loses exactly half of the removed original mass. Supporting traces may
occur on UNCHANGED fibers; they do not enter (4).

Combining (1) and (4) yields the exact response

    int_boundary(W-beta)v=(1/2-beta)D.                 (5)

Hence, if beta<1/2, no stress with this geometric cap menu can satisfy

    int_boundary(W-beta)Phi<=0

for every nonnegative convex physical test Phi. Equation (2) supplies a
finite convex test with strictly positive response. This is a proved
geometric exclusion, not a presumed transfer between surface and volume
transport measures.

The limiting stress need NOT have a finite menu for this argument. Suppose
instead that Lambda is one probability measure on actual cap records and
s_H is its disintegrated actual boundary selector. If, for Lambda-almost
every nonvertical cap and almost every X in every moving B_z, its plane
lies strictly between the paired roof points, the selector is the ordinary
indicator at both points. Tonelli then gives (4) for
W=int s_H dLambda, and (5) follows unchanged. No uniform crossing margin
over the cap law is required for this limiting response statement. Such a
margin was used above only for exact finite-t cap-loss assertions on a
finite menu. The joint record/disintegration theorem in
candidate 714f69e684c396b1
provides a precise interface for these actual limiting selectors; it does
not by itself prove the additional crossing condition.

If atomic rows have total weight eta_A, let A(z) be their total captured
weight at base z, and let the proper menu have weight1-eta_A. The response
is instead exactly

    sum_z h_z |B_z| [1-eta_A+2A(z)-2beta].              (6)

Thus the same exclusion holds whenever their ACTUAL weighted roof credit
satisfies

    sum h_z|B_z| A(z) >= (eta_A/2)sum h_z|B_z|.

Atomic rows cannot simply be dropped when this condition is unavailable.

## 3. An actual descent for the ordinary rectangle calibration

Set eta=1/200 and use widths

    r=(1,51/50,51/50,203/200,101/100)

on bases -2,-1,0,1,2. Put a=3/800 and

    h(z)=min{3(z+2),2-z},
    H(z)=1+a h(z).

The sampled halfheights are

    H=(1,809/800,403/400,803/800,1).

Both width and height roofs are concave, so these are actual compatible
rectangles. At the ordinary source (0,0,0), the exact all-normal cap
certificate gives

    Q=812869/160000,
    M=814069/80000,
    M-2Q=3/200>0.                                    (7)

The only minimizing orientations there are +/-y-z/2>=0. The verification
uses the same complete exact clipping/Bernstein procedure as the buffered
rectangle theorem, now with zero buffer:43 cells per base-tilt sign and
138 triangles, all six quadratic Bernstein coefficients nonnegative.
Every zero face lies on a coordinate axis; the two axis tables identify
the stated minimum. Other bases have strict pure-base upper bounds below
Q. The two vertical caps cover the entire source fiber. Consequently the
global ordinary depth is Q, without requiring uniqueness of its mark.

For completeness, the exact clipping input for an oblique cap
tx+uy+s b z>=0 (t,u>0, b>=0, s=+/-1) is

    2tu*capmass = sum_z [(s b z+H_z u+r_z t/2)_+^2
                        -(s b z+H_z u-r_z t/2)_+^2
                        -(s b z-H_z u+r_z t/2)_+^2
                        +(s b z-H_z u-r_z t/2)_+^2].

Normalize t+u+b=1. The verifier successively clips this triangle by all
twenty displayed linear forms, forms the exact quadratic after subtracting
2tuQ, and checks every degree-two Bernstein coefficient on its fan
triangulation. This is the full all-normal procedure proved in
candidate 79b44436a463e3c4,
Sections3--4, with the present heights and zero buffer. The vertical and
horizontal axis formulas are respectively

    sum_z r_z clamp(H_z+a z,0,2H_z),
    sum_z 2H_z clamp(r_z/2+a z,0,r_z).

Their complete finite breakpoint lists, including both constant unbounded
tails, are checked. Closed pure-base caps through0 contain the own fiber
and one whole side; their masses exceed Q as well.

Now decrease a to a-t, with 0<t<a. This is an actual compatible nested
body motion of the form in Section1, with b_1=3(z+2), b_2=2-z. Its sampled
speed is h=(0,3,2,1,0). Both displayed critical caps cut all three moving
prisms properly, while their endpoint inside/outside facets are unchanged.
Writing

    A=3r_-1+2r_0+r_1=1223/200,

their masses and the whole original mass change EXACTLY as

    Q_t=Q-At,       M_t=M-2At.                         (8)

The old pure-base gaps at all other bases persist for sufficiently small
t. The two fixed vertical caps still cover the entire own fiber, so the
NEW actual global maximum is at most Q_t. Equations (7)--(8) give

    Q_t/M_t-Q/M=At(2Q-M)/[M(M-2At)]<0.                 (9)

Thus this is an actual strict body descent of the globally deepest
inside-facet calibration. It identifies a specific additional geometric
obligation imposed by joint body optimality, beyond fixed-body parameter
optimality. Neither the surface row nor the volume row is relabeled as
the other one.

## 4. Exact scope of the proposed structural test

For a candidate limiting prism family and a retained actual cap menu,
the next finite test is to find affine roof-plane velocities b_r with:

* a genuine nested positive roof motion and D>0;
* strict proper crossing of every positive-weight cap on every moving
  prism, or a directly verified replacement for the trace identity (4);
* the actual atomic credit in (6), if atomic weights remain.

If such velocities exist, the limiting ordinary convex stress is
impossible at beta<1/2 by (2)--(5). Checking those conditions is a genuine
geometric feasibility problem, not merely the original OC inequality
restated as an unknown scalar payment.

There is no automatic existence claim. For example a constant height
roof H=1 over a chain has no nonzero inward perturbation supported only
at interior bases that preserves concavity while fixing both endpoint
heights: concavity forces H_t>=1 between the fixed endpoints, whereas
inwardness gives H_t<=1. Nor does a weak measure omega<=dS alone imply the
paired trace identity (4). These are explicit retained limitations.

## 5. Exact verification

Run python3 work/verify_paired_roof_half_loss_two_sided.py. It reconstructs
the zero-buffer clipping arrangement from the actual heights and passes
1,587 exact checks (86 cells, 138 triangles). Its imported, previously
audited clipping utilities first replay the 1,529-check buffered
certificate. The new checks also verify the exact masses, all axis
statuses, cap-loss identities, concavity, and strict normalized descent.
The analytic paired-roof theorem and the convex-penalty limit are proved
above; those assertions are not inferred from finitely many samples.
